key_insight: AI-generated synthetic tabular data closely matched real dyslipidemia cardiovascular-prevention datasets and preserved key clinical associations.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic data may enable safer, faster exploratory research and model development when real-world clinical data are difficult to access.
method: Fine-tuned pre-trained LLMs on original clinical records to generate synthetic tabular data.
Compared synthetic vs. real datasets using fidelity and privacy metrics.
Benchmarked performance against traditional anonymization methods within secure institutional infrastructure.
evidence_signal: Synthetic datasets showed strong agreement with the originals, with meaningful differences limited to a few variables and key predictive relationships largely preserved.
watch_item: Some effect sizes were slightly attenuated, so synthetic data should be validated before use for confirmatory analysis or high-stakes decisions.
paper_title: Evaluation of AI-Generated Synthetic Data for Clinical Research in Secondary Cardiovascular Prevention among Dyslipidemia Patients
